item.title: AI‑altered White House renovation photo posted by Donald Trump flagged by Google detector
item.description:
AI‑altered White House renovation photo posted by Donald Trump flagged by Google detector

President Donald Trump posted a series of photos on Truth Social showing off renovations to the White House — but one of them appears to be modified with AI.

🔍 Overview

  • The post includes a “before and after” photo of a freshly painted White House column.
  • The image was shared to brag about White House restoration work.

🧩 Detection

  • Google’s AI detector flagged the picture as “made or edited with OpenAI.”
  • The Verge confirmed the photo is flagged as AI‑generated when uploaded to Google’s SynthID Detector, which scans for an invisible watermark indicating it was “created or edited” with AI.
  • The SynthID watermark was not detected on other pictures Trump posted, which show the White House façade and heliport.

⚙️ Visual anomalies

  • Reddit users noted an uneven number of steps on both sides of the structure.
  • The number of steps does not match the ones in the “before” photo.
  • The before and after photos appear nearly identical in angle and detail; the reflection in the windows is nearly the same, and the protective cardboard at the bottom of the column seems to be in the same spot as well.
  • The “newly‑painted” column looks unnaturally smooth.

📚 Context

  • Real pictures show people painting the front of the White House in June, so it’s possible the column actually did get a fresh coat of paint — the White House didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.
  • Trump is no stranger to AI tools, as he often posts AI‑generated caricatures of himself.
  • The White House has previously posted racist AI memes and at least one photo deceptively edited to make a protester appear distraught.

#AI #Deepfake #Trump #WhiteHouse

Source: Trump posts AI-edited photo to brag about White House restoration work

item.title: White House Launches Super Intelligence Force AI Task Force Led by Jay Clayton
item.description:
White House Launches Super Intelligence Force AI Task Force Led by Jay Clayton

The White House has established a new artificial intelligence task force, named the “Super Intelligence Force,” to evaluate the risks and opportunities of the rapidly advancing technology. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton has been appointed to lead the panel and deliver federal oversight recommendations within 120 days.

🔍 Overview

The creation of the task force follows a Tuesday meeting between President Donald Trump and prominent technology executives, including OpenAI President Greg Brockman, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. During the meeting, President Trump secured a “morally binding” agreement from the heads of major US tech companies to implement internal safety monitoring and independent external reviews of their AI systems.

⚙️ Key Details

The “Super Intelligence Force” will evaluate how existing laws and potential congressional actions can address emerging AI threats. Key elements of the task force’s mandate include:

  • Oversight Recommendations: Delivering recommendations on federal oversight within a 120-day window.
  • Protecting Innovation: Examining how existing laws might address emerging threats without imposing regulatory burdens that hinder competition or stifle innovation.
  • Industry Collaboration: Collaborating directly with industry leaders to identify system vulnerabilities.
  • Voluntary Standards: Developing response strategies for advanced AI threats while maintaining American technological leadership through voluntary standards rather than mandatory federal restrictions.

🛡️ Incident Reporting Review

The task force is also charged with reviewing and improving security protocols. The panel will:

  • Review current protocols for reporting breaches, hacks, and model jailbreaks to federal authorities.
  • Recommend improvements to these reporting procedures under existing legal frameworks.

#ArtificialIntelligence #WhiteHouse #AIGovernance #TechPolicy

Source: White House forms task force to assess AI risks: WSJ
